chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'You prompt your dying ones at the time of death with "There is no god but Allah," while we prompt our dying ones with "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family."'

key_terms.تلقين: Talqeen — the practice of prompting a dying or recently deceased person with the articles of faith
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: The first shahada — 'There is no god but Allah'
key_terms.محمد رسول الله: The second shahada — 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'
key_terms.موتاكم: Your dying ones — those in the throes of death

ai.seo_question: What should be recited during talqeen (prompting the dying) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Two Imams — Imam al-Baqir (AS) and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — transmitted this ruling on talqeen (prompting the dying person). The narration highlights a distinction: while others recite only the first part of the shahada (lā ilāha illā Allāh) to the dying, the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt also recite the second part (Muḥammadun rasūl Allāh). This underscores the Shia emphasis on the complete shahada — including recognition of the Prophet's messengership — as an essential expression of faith at the moment of death. The inclusion of both Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq in the chain lends the ruling exceptional authority.
